title: Pugachev's Rebellion
text: Pugachev's Rebellion of 1773–1775 was the principal revolt in a series of popular rebellions that took place in the Russian Empire after Catherine II, known today as Catherine the Great, seized power in 1762. It began as an organized insurrection of Yaik Cossacks headed by Yemelyan Pugachev, a disaffected ex-lieutenant of the Imperial Russian Army, against a background of profound peasant unrest and war with the Ottoman Empire. After initial success, Pugachev assumed leadership of an alternative government, claiming to be Catherine's late husband Tsar Peter III and proclaiming an end to serfdom. This organized leadership presented a challenge to the imperial administration of Catherine II.
